events_chronological: Saxophonist Alden Frey suspects his wife Lorna of an affair and cannot reach her in bed or anywhere else.
Unmarked tapes begin turning up at the door, showing first the outside of the house, then its rooms, then the two of them asleep.
At a party Alden meets a pale stranger who tells him he is inside Alden's house at that moment and hands him a phone that proves it.
A tape arrives showing Alden standing over Lorna's dismembered body.
Alden is convicted of her murder and put on death row.
Blinding headaches take hold in the cell, and one morning Alden is gone and a young mechanic named Cully Boone is in his place.
Baffled police release Cully to his parents, who will not say what they saw the night he appeared.
Cully goes back to work at the garage, where the gangster Mr. Vance is a favoured customer.
Mr. Vance brings his girlfriend Sunny Keele, Lorna's double as a blonde, to the garage, and she and Cully begin an affair.
Sunny tells Cully that Mr. Vance - the pornographer Rolf Dane - forced her into his films at gunpoint.
Mr. Vance telephones Cully and puts the pale stranger on to explain what happens to men who sleep with his girlfriend.
Sunny talks Cully into robbing and killing the fence Perry so the two of them can run.
Cully kills Perry by accident and sees a photograph of Sunny and Lorna together in Mr. Vance's world.
Sunny and Cully drive to a cabin in the desert and have sex on the sand, and she tells him he will never have her.
Sunny walks into the cabin and the man who stands up outside is Alden Frey again.
The pale stranger films Alden at the cabin and tells him that the woman's name is Lorna.
Alden takes Mr. Vance into the desert, cuts his throat with the stranger's help, and is shown a screen playing his own life back at him.
Alden drives to his own house and speaks into the intercom the words the film opened with: "Rolf Dane is dead."
The police give chase down the road as Alden's face distorts and the film ends where it began.
nonlinear_category_reason: Forward throughout apart from the opening, which is the later scene the loop closes on.
syuzhet_notes: The film is a closed loop: told-order bullet 1 is the husband hearing through his own intercom the message that told-order bullet 18 shows him delivering, so the first scene is caused by the second-to-last. Apart from that closure the telling runs forward, but it runs forward through a transformation that swaps one protagonist for another at told-order bullet 7 and swaps back at bullet 16, leaving the two halves impossible to lay on one timeline with any confidence.
fabula_notes: The film offers no account of the transformation, so this chronology treats it as literal succession, which is one reading among several; the common alternative is that the mechanic material is a fugue constructed on death row, in which case bullets 7-15 are not later than bullets 5-6 but simultaneous with them. Whether the two women are the same woman is deliberately unresolved.
